<description>
**Problem:** Block preparation inserts an unused final transaction ID, repeatedly constructs salted transaction-ID sets, and allocates a worker-task vector. Small input queues also submit more tasks than can do useful work.

**Fix:** Insert each transaction ID before scanning the following transaction's inputs. Reuse the set's buckets and hash salt and the worker-task vector across blocks. Limit submitted tasks to the smaller of the worker and queued-input counts.

Besides the simplifications this also results in a 1% validation speedup.
</description>

The vector is cast to an r-value reference. (The template type becoming an l-value is banned through `!std::is_lvalue_reference_v<R>`).
The argument to `Submit()` is never used to construct a new vector inside the method, which means the storage of the underlying vector is never currently "reaped".
My inference is that the `ThreadPool` was written that way since we move from the individual *elements* of the range.

It would probably be more honest/correct to allow non-const l-values to be passed into `Submit()` and remove the `move()` here. `!std::is_const_v<std::remove_reference_t<R>>` could be sufficient, and the l-value/r-value nature of `R` would be up to the caller as was intended when r-value references were introduced.
